function: Near-field beam training (codeword prediction with angle and distance) and beam tracking for XL-MIMO analog beamforming; CNN predicts the best codeword, LSTM tracks it, pp. 2-4.
system: Downlink XL-MIMO: BS with 512-antenna half-wavelength ULA and analog beamforming, single-antenna UE, 50 GHz mmWave, near-field; no RIS, pp. 1, 4.
method: Supervised learning, offline: two-stage CNN with inception blocks classifying the optimal codeword (cross-entropy); CNN plus LSTM for tracking, pp. 3-4.
data_channel: Self-generated simulated dataset of 50,000 samples: near-field channel with one LoS and two NLoS paths, UE angle U(-90,90) degrees, distance U(13,100) m; no real data, p. 4.
test_conditions: Offline training on 80% of the simulated set, testing on the held-out 20% from the same distribution; SNR 0-15 dB; tracking T=10 periods, speeds U(3,17) m/s, pp. 4-5.
baselines: Non-learned: hierarchical spatial-chirp scheme [8], exhaustive beam sweeping upper bound. Learned: original and improved DL schemes [9]. Ablation: CTNBT with standard CNN block, pp. 5-6.
metrics: Normalized gain, achievable rate (bps/Hz), beam training overhead (codewords tested), effect of tracking length T, pp. 5-6.
complexity: Asymptotic order O(.) of CTNBT and LNBT in layer sizes, kernel sizes, batch size and codebook sizes; no runtime or FLOPs, p. 4.
openness: none; dataset generated by simulation, no code or data link, p. 4.
q1_support: p. 4: "we generate the dataset by simulations", after "the existing real world trajectory datasets cannot provide the denoised channel". Custom near-field simulator with one LoS and two NLoS paths; no 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 4: "the dataset has 50,000 entries, with 80% of data used for training and 20% of data used" for testing; p. 5: "we evaluate the LNBT with T = 2, 3". Held-out split of the same simulated distribution plus SNR and T sweeps; nothing states a trained model meets an unseen scenario.
q3_support: p. 5: "the original scheme [9], the improved scheme [9], and the hierarchical scheme [8]" compared on normalized gain (Fig. 4) and achievable rate (Fig. 5); p. 6: [9] is "Deep learning based beam training for extremely large-scale massive MIMO in near-field domain". [8] and beam sweeping are non-learned.
q4_support: p. 4: "complexity of the mth hidden layer can be denoted as" O(...); the total orders of CTNBT and LNBT are then given in terms of N(1), Ne, T, layer sizes and kernel sizes.
q5_support: p. 4: "we generate the dataset by simulations". No link or DOI to code or data is given, and no public dataset is used.
notes: Included, area 3: the learned method selects and tracks the beam (codeword) and is judged by normalized gain and achievable rate; the angle and distance of the UE are a by-product, not a localization task. [9] is taken as learned from its title in the reference list (p. 6). q2 is borderline: Fig. 6 (p. 5) sweeps T=2 to 20 while p. 4 sets T=10 for the dataset, but the paper does not say whether the LSTM is reused or retrained, so 0.
